name: application-number-format-preview
title: Number Format Preview
description: Locale-aware number/currency/date preview rows computed live via Intl.NumberFormat and Intl.DateTimeFormat — distinct from currency-input, which is an editable single-locale input rather than a read-only multi-locale comparison of the same underlying value.
useWhen: Letting a developer or translator preview how the same value renders across multiple locales.
You want the formatted output computed live via Intl APIs rather than hand-typed per locale.
Reviewing RTL locale output (e.g. Arabic) alongside LTR locales for a formatting QA pass.
avoidWhen: You need an editable currency input for a single locale — use currency-input instead.
You only support one locale — locale-comparison rows add unnecessary complexity.
You need full RTL page mirroring, not just RTL text within cells — use a dedicated RTL layout demo instead.
responsiveBehavior: The table has a fixed max width; on narrow viewports it should be wrapped in a horizontally scrollable container by the consuming page.
accessibility: RTL locale cells carry dir='rtl' so digit and text ordering render correctly and are announced in the right order by screen readers.
Every value is generated from the same real amount and date via Intl formatters, so no locale row can drift out of sync with the others.
Locale codes are shown in monospace to visually distinguish them from the formatted output.

variants.title: Number format preview
variants.description: The same $1,234,567.89 amount and August 8, 2026 date formatted across en-US, de-DE, ja-JP, and ar-EG (RTL) locales via real Intl output, on a light surface.
accessibility: All four rows are generated by calling Intl.NumberFormat/Intl.DateTimeFormat with the same amount and date, verified against real Node.js Intl output before being hand-transcribed into the static HTML example.

variants.title: Number format preview (Dark)
variants.description: The same four-locale preview, adapted for dark surfaces.
accessibility: Text meets WCAG AA contrast on dark backgrounds, including RTL Arabic-Indic digit glyphs.
